description: Structured logging, log aggregation, ELK/EFK stack, and logging best practices for distributed Java systems

questions.question: What is structured logging and why is it important for microservices?
questions.answer: Structured logging outputs logs as structured data (JSON) instead of plain text. Important for microservices because: 1) Machine-parseable - easy aggregation and search, 2) Consistent format across services, 3) Rich context with fields, 4) Correlation IDs for distributed tracing. Example plain text: '2024-03-29 10:15:30 ERROR Payment failed for order 12345'. Structured: {'timestamp':'2024-03-29T10:15:30Z','level':'ERROR','message':'Payment failed','orderId':'12345','userId':'user-789','correlationId':'abc-123','service':'payment','error':'InsufficientFunds'}. Search all errors for user: userId='user-789' AND level='ERROR'. Trace request: correlationId='abc-123'. Implementation with Logback and Logstash encoder enables JSON output, searchable in Elasticsearch, visualizable in Kibana.
